text:
anna: Heads up — we have 3 failed restore attempts for tenant-123 snapshots from archive bucket. Error in restore logs: 'decrypt: missing-encrypt-header'. Anyone seen this pattern before?

devon: I saw one of those alerts. Quick look at object metadata — header shows x-enc-meta: sse-c but our policy expects aws:kms / CMK.

marco: That coincides with yesterday's uploader RBAC tweak. @lina, did the change alter any secret access for the uploader svcacct?

lina: We removed one broad iam:secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission and scoped it down. I didn't think it would break default encryption, but will pull the diff now.

anna: Timestamp on failures ~2026-03-21T02:03:10Z and started spiking for ~15m after the deploy.

devon: Audit logs show PutObject events, but I don't see KMS GenerateDataKey or KMS Encrypt events tied. Looks like the upload path fell back to client-side SSE-C instead of CMK rewrap.

restore-bot: restore attempt tenant-123/snap-20260321 -> FAILED.

```
restore-bot: restore tenant-123-snap-20260321
error: KMS.DecryptDenied: grant missing
s3 metadata: x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256
x-enc-meta: sse-c
```

lina: Oh — our v2.3.1 uploader change introduced a fallback to SSE-C when KMS env var is missing. The RBAC change likely prevented it from reading the secret so it defaulted. That's on me, sorry.

devon: So root cause = RBAC scope reduction + uploader fallback bug. Immediate risk: customers' blobs stored with client-provided keys (SSE-C) which we cannot decrypt unless we have those client keys. We need to identify all affected objects and enable restores where possible.

marco: Mitigations: 1) block further uploads from that uploader version 2) remove fallback behavior via a feature flag 3) detect objects with x-enc-meta: sse-c and mark for manual handling.

anna: For current restore backlog, can we create an ephemeral KMS grant to allow decrypts? We need to be careful and record who created it.

devon: We can, but only helps if object was encrypted with our CMK. If it's SSE-C with a client key never stored here, grant won't help. For objects with missing rewrap (i.e., uploader didn't KMS-encrypt), we'll need uploader to surface keys or restore from source. For those where uploader did call KMS but grant timing failed, ephemeral grant will help.

marco: I'll try to reproduce decrypt failure locally. Proposed quick commands for the grant approach:

```
# create short-lived grant
kmscli grant create --key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd1234 --grantee restore-runner --ttl 3600 --purpose DECRYPT
# use grant id to attempt decrypt
aws s3 cp s3://archive/tenant-123/snap-20260321 ./tmp && kmscli decrypt --grant <grant-id> --in ./tmp --out ./plain
# retire grant after use
kmscli grant retire --id <grant-id>
```

lina: I'm opening an approval request to sec-ops and oncall for ephemeral grant creation. Adding audit note: must record issuer principal + ticket link before grant creation.

sre-bot: Incident INC-20260321 created: https://incidents.internal/INC-20260321 — severity P2, owner: eng-security.

devon: Detection task — I'll run a head-object batch for tenant-123 keys to enumerate x-enc-meta. Inventory won't have custom metadata so need parallel head calls or lambda. Quick pseudo: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket archive --prefix tenant-123/ | jq -r .Contents[].Key | xargs -n1 -P10 aws s3api head-object --bucket archive --key`

marco: I'll reserve 1 hour to run the head-object sweep and generate CSV of offending keys. I'll also attempt one manual decrypt with ephemeral grant if sec approves.

lina: Long-term fixes: 1) CI gate that validates uploader sets x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms 2) remove SSE-C fallback in uploader 3) reintroduce a secrets access smoke test to catch env propagation.

anna: Compliance note — if any client-provided keys are present or were exfiltrated, we must notify SOC/legal. @lina please include timeline, list of keys/objects, and whether any external IPs were involved.

devon: Audit logs show uploader traffic from internal instances only. No unknown IPs so far, but will dig deeper.

lina: I'll prepare the RBAC diff + commit that caused the reduced secret permission and attach it to the incident.

anna: Action owners: devon -> detection script & audit correlation; marco -> run head-object sweep + temp restores; lina -> RBAC rollback patch + timeline; anna -> compliance/incident comms.

marco: ETA for initial list: 45 minutes.

devon: Quick FYI — I'll add a Live Query to detect any future uploads missing aws:kms in headers.

anna: Thanks all. Keep updates to the incident thread. We'll draft a short postmortem after containment. :thumbsup:
